query: Which ML methods and uncertainty metrics (calibration, credible intervals, coverage) are appropriate for entity resolution and imputation when linking BOMs across systems?

response.query: Which ML methods and uncertainty metrics (calibration, credible intervals, coverage) are appropriate for entity resolution and imputation when linking BOMs across systems?
response.answer: Machine learning methods like ensemble models and neural networks are suitable for entity resolution. Uncertainty metrics like calibration, credible intervals, and coverage are appropriate for assessing model reliability in imputation tasks.

results.title: 2025 Spotlight Posters - ICML 2026
results.content: Zhangyi Liu ⋅ Feng Liu ⋅ Rui Gao ⋅ Shuang Li. Jul 15, 11:00 AM - 1:30 PM    West Exhibition Hall B2-B3. We study convergence properties of the discrete-time Mean-Field Langevin Stochastic Descent-Ascent (MFL-SDA) algorithm for solving distributional minimax optimization. These problems arise in various applications, such as zero-sum games, generative adversarial networks and distributionally robust learning. Despite the significance of MFL-SDA in these contexts, the discrete-time convergence rate remains underexplored.To address this gap, we establish a last-iterate convergence rate of $O(\frac{1}{\epsilon}\log\frac{1}{\epsilon})$ for MFL-SDA. This rate is nearly optimal when compared to the complexity lower bound of its Euclidean counterpart. This rate also matches the complexity of mean-field Langevin stochastic gradient descent for distributional minimization and the outer-loop iteration complexity of an existing double-loop algorithm for distributional minimax problems.By leveraging an elementary analysis framework that avoids PDE-based techniques, we overcome previous limitations and achieve a faster convergence rate.
